author: Pontoppidan, 1763
habitat: 갯벌, 강 하구, 물 고인 논
summary: 해마다 봄과 가을에 수천 마리가 지나가는 나그네새다. 갯벌이나 강 하구, 물 고인 논에서 홀로 또는 2~5마리씩 작은 무리로 지내며, 민물도요나 좀도요 무리에 섞이기도 한다. 갑각류, 조개류, 환형동물과 함께 식물 열매도 먹는다. 스칸디나비아반도 북부, 러시아 서북부, 시베리아 동북부에서 번식하며 마른풀이나 마른 잎을 깐 접시 모양 둥지에 알 4개를 낳고, 겨울은 중동, 인도, 동남아시아, 호주에서 난다.

art.subject: Broad-billed Sandpiper (Calidris falcinellus), adult in breeding plumage as seen on Korean tidal flats in May: dark brown crown with a narrow pale lateral crown-stripe above a white supercilium, so that two whitish stripes (a split supercilium) run above the eye, with a dark eye-stripe below; upperparts blackish-brown, the feathers fringed rufous-buff and white, forming whitish lines along the mantle and scapulars like a small snipe; neck, foreneck and breast whitish, densely streaked dark brown, the streaks extending as chevrons onto the flanks; belly white. Bill blackish; dark eye; legs dark greyish-olive.
art.pose: feeding on wet mud among other small sandpipers
art.scene: Korean tidal flat at a river mouth during spring migration in May; no people, buildings or text
views: adult breeding plumage (May), side view standing: split whitish supercilium with a dark crown and eye-stripe, blackish-brown upperparts with rufous and white fringes forming pale lines on the back, densely streaked neck and breast with chevrons on the flanks, white belly, long bill kinked down near the tip

adult non-breeding plumage, side view standing: grey-brown upperparts with dark centres and dark shaft streaks to each feather, split whitish supercilium still visible, finely streaked grey breast, white underparts
in flight seen from above: narrow white wing-bar, blackish rump, uppertail coverts and central tail, white sides to the rump
art.build: Small, low-slung sandpiper, 17cm, a little larger than a sparrow and slightly smaller than a Dunlin, with short legs and a rather hunched, crouching feeding stance. Bill blackish, longer than the head, broad and flattened at the base, straight for most of its length and then kinked downward just before the tip. Legs short, dark. At rest the wingtips reach about the tail tip. In flight a narrow white wing-bar and a blackish centre to the rump and tail with white sides.
avoid: Do not paint a single plain supercilium; it is split into two pale stripes above the eye.
Do not paint an evenly curved bill (Curlew Sandpiper) or a short stint bill; it is long, broad-based, straight, with a downward kink at the tip.
Do not paint yellow or long legs; they are short and dark.
Do not paint a black belly patch (Dunlin); the belly is white.
